A.summary: Evil is not a privation, because evil has degrees and privation does not.

B.summary: Evil is a privation, because privation admits of degrees as distance from the good, and does not exist in itself.

c1.text: Privation does not admit of more or less.

c2.text: Existence admits of more or less, since there can be degrees of perfection in existence.

c3.text: Among evil things, some are more evil than others (evil admits of degrees).

c6.text: When something is more or less evil, it refers to how far removed it is from the good.

c7.text: Concepts involving privation, such as inequality or dissimilarity, admit of more or less as distance from equality or similarity.

c8.text: Privation admits of more or less.

c9.text: A privation is not a property that exists in itself, but only increases or decreases according to the cause that produces it.

c10.text: Good can exist without evil, but evil cannot exist without good.

a.note: Unlike A, B holds that evil is a privation.

b.note: A acknowledges degrees of evil as a premise, and B agrees with it.

c.note: B supports the asymmetrical dependence of evil on good via privation (c9), whereas A views evil as an independent existence.
